name: Hippocampal Relational Binding and Encoding
short_description: Hippocampus transforms experience into memory through relational binding; encoding strength driven by CA1 prediction error, modulated by emotional arousal, schema congruence, and attention
higher_order_principle: The hippocampus transforms experience into memory through relational binding — creating conjunctive representations that link the what (item information from LEC/perirhinal), where (spatial context from MEC/parahippocampal), and when (temporal context from MEC time cells) of an experience. Encoding strength is driven by prediction error (CA1 mismatch detection), modulated by emotional arousal (amygdala), schema congruence (vmPFC), and attention (prefrontal gating). Encoding that generates PE produces stronger, more durable memory traces than encoding that confirms predictions.

input_pathways.where: MEC → parahippocampal → spatial context, scene layout
input_pathways.when: MEC time cells → temporal context, sequence position

processing_stages.entorhinal_cortex: receives convergent input from neocortical association areas
processing_stages.dentate_gyrus: pattern separation — making similar inputs more dissimilar
processing_stages.CA3: pattern completion — reactivating full pattern from partial cue
processing_stages.CA1: mismatch detection between retrieved and current input

neural_substrate.output: conjunctive episodic trace binding all elements

causal_links.evidence_base: Davachi, 2006; Kumaran & Maguire, 2006; Chen et al., 2015

parameters.mechanism: CA1 receives current input (entorhinal) and retrieved pattern (CA3). Mismatch = PE = encoding signal.
parameters.high_PE: strongly engages encoding — novel, surprising, schema-violating information
parameters.low_PE: weakly engages encoding — familiar, expected, schema-congruent information
parameters.educational_implication: PASSIVE re-exposure generates LOW PE → POOR encoding. ACTIVE prediction/generation generates HIGH PE → STRONG encoding.

parameters.critical_property: trace is CONTEXT-DEPENDENT — retrieval requires matching context cues

parameters.mechanism: amygdala → hippocampus direct projections enhance LTP

inverted_U.moderate_arousal: OPTIMAL encoding (curiosity, mild surprise, personal relevance)
inverted_U.high_arousal: impaired HIPPOCAMPAL encoding but enhanced AMYGDALA encoding (fragmented, emotional-gist memory — the test anxiety pattern)

causal_links.evidence_base: van Kesteren et al., 2012; Tse et al., 2007

parameters.schema_congruent: vmPFC detects fit → partial hippocampal bypass → fast neocortical integration
parameters.schema_incongruent: vmPFC detects violation → STRONG hippocampal encoding (PE signal)
parameters.schema_irrelevant: no schema activated → weak encoding on all pathways

parameters.mechanism: MEC time cells provide slowly drifting context signal. Items encoded close in time share similar context → become associated.

educational_implication.spacing: different temporal contexts → more retrieval routes → better retention
educational_implication.interleaving: different category items in each temporal context → forces content-based rather than context-based discrimination

scope_conditions: Encoding requires ATTENTION — hippocampal encoding is sharply reduced when attention is divided (Uncapher & Rugg, 2005)
Encoding is enhanced by GENERATION — producing an answer (even an incorrect one) generates stronger PE than passively receiving the answer
Encoding is enhanced by ELABORATION — connecting new information to existing knowledge creates more retrieval routes
Age modulates encoding: hippocampal encoding is robust from early childhood; prefrontal control matures slowly through adolescence

interactions.nature: ED1 creates bound traces; ED2's pattern separation ensures similar episodes are distinguishable.
Schema congruence in ED1 determines which encoding pathway (ED4) is engaged.
CA1 mismatch detection is a specific instance of the general prediction error mechanism in T1.

ecological_testability: HIGH — subsequent memory paradigm (DM effect) measurable by fMRI; behavioral encoding strength measurable by delayed test; attention measurable by dual-task interference.
